theorem_title: Every sensor in a tail has a large gauge-fixed witness
natural_language_statement:
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and $x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb Z^2$, define the observation $r_n(x)=x_1+(n+1)x_2$, target $q(x)=x_1$, and witness $w_n=(n+1,-1)$. For any natural offset $O$ and index $j$,

$$
r_{O+j}(w_{O+j})=0,\qquad (w_{O+j})_2=-1,\qquad q(w_{O+j})>O.
$$

The lower bound is uniform over the tail indices. Each sensor has its own witness; no single direction annihilating the entire tail is asserted.
formal_statement:
theorem NewMathDiscovery.LinearBlindness.RankTwoInstability.tail_witnesses_uniformly_large (offset index : Nat) :
    observe (offset + index) (witness (offset + index)) = 0 ∧
    (witness (offset + index)).2 = -1 ∧
    target (witness (offset + index)) > Int.ofNat offset := by sorry
